title: Nike, PayPal, Adobe, Netflix, PepsiCo: Which Is Actually Cheap Now?
creator: The German Value Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble several names and figures in places
summary: The German Value Investor runs his scenario calculator over five well-known stocks that have all fallen sharply; he recently bought three of them himself. Nike is down nearly 80% from its 2021 high of about $180, margins collapsed from 10-13% to about 5%, and the brand is losing customers; his scenario grade is 3.07. Fair price about $30, buy limit $21: NKE HOLD reiterated, on the sidelines. PepsiCo is down about 30% from its 2023 high, back to about $140; a dividend aristocrat yielding over 4%, but barely growing and highly indebted at $33 of net debt per share. Fair price $80, buy limit $55: PEP HOLD, flipping from SELL on 18 October. Netflix is down over 50% from $115 to about $60; it is losing US customers monthly but raising prices faster than churn costs it, showing pricing power, with good margins and almost no net debt. Fair price over 40% above today's price, margin-of-safety $67, buy limit $57: NFLX BUY reiterated; he holds 1.3% and may add. Adobe is down 65% from its high but posting record revenue and profits despite AI fears, at a 13x adjusted P/E with heavy buybacks; even his negative case is only about 20% downside against over 60% upside normally. Buy limit $270 against a ~$240 price: ADBE BUY reiterated; he holds 3.3% and may buy more. PayPal is his largest position at 16%, up 7%, at about a 10x P/E, forecast raised slightly, buybacks absorbing over 10% of shares a year: PYPL BUY, first tracked for him, buy limit just under $60.
